why: XOR of the whole array cancels all pairs and leaves a ^ b. Any set bit of a ^ b (take the lowest, x & -x) is a bit where a and b differ, so splitting the array by that bit puts a and b in different halves, and XOR-ing each half recovers them.
hints: XOR everything. What do you get, and why is it not zero?
You get a ^ b, which is nonzero because a != b. A 1-bit in it is a position where a and b differ.
low = x & -x; XOR together all v with v & low; that is a; b = x ^ a. Return them sorted. O(n), O(1) space.
pitfalls: Return the two values in ascending order.
In fixed-width languages x & -x overflows for the minimum integer; Python is fine.
Negative numbers work because XOR acts on two's-complement bits.
